This PR primarily clarifies the `openclaw message` documentation (English and Chinese) to distinguish core built-in channel surfaces from plugin-provided channels, and adds a note that plugin channels may also expose `openclaw message` support. It also contains an unrelated change removing the `"skills": ["./skills"]` entry from the feishu plugin manifest and its generated metadata counterpart.\n\n**Key concerns:**\n- **Unintentional skills regression (P1):** `"skills": ["./skills"]` is removed from `extensions/feishu/openclaw.plugin.json` and the generated `bundled-plugin-metadata.generated.ts`, even though the `./skills` directory still contains four active skill definitions (`feishu-doc`, `feishu-drive`, `feishu-perm`, `feishu-wiki`). Greptile Summary

This PR adds documentation to `docs/channels/feishu.md` and `docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md` to explain the Feishu routing fallback chain and session key format. The intent is worthwhile — closing a diagnostics gap noted in issue #54952 — but both changed files contain the same factual inaccuracy about the role of `groupPolicy`. **Key issues:** - **Inaccurate agent-selection claim (both files):** `channels.defaults.groupPolicy` is an access-control mechanism (`open` / `allowlist` / `disabled`) that determines whether a group message is accepted, not which agent handles it. The added text in `feishu.md` says it is applied "to determine which agent handles it," and the `configuration-reference.md` addition says it is used "to select the handling agent." Both phrases are incorrect and could mislead operators trying to debug wrong-agent routing. The actual agent selection in the fallback path is governed by `channels.feishu.defaultAccount` (already mentioned correctly in the same sentence in `feishu.md`). - The session-key and fallback-chain concepts themselves are a good addition, but the `groupPolicy` role needs to be corrected in both files before this lands.

Confidence Score: 3/5

Not safe to merge as-is — both files contain a factual inaccuracy about `groupPolicy` that would mislead operators debugging routing issues. The fallback-chain and session-key additions are directionally correct and address a real documentation gap, but the same incorrect claim (that `groupPolicy` selects the handling agent) appears in both changed files. Since this is an operator-facing debugging aid, publishing inaccurate information about how agent selection works would actively harm the users this PR is trying to help. A targeted correction to the `groupPolicy` description in both files is needed before landing. Both `docs/channels/feishu.md` (line 608) and `docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md` (line 86) need the `groupPolicy` agent-selection language corrected.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | docs/channels/feishu.md | Adds a fallback-chain paragraph under 'Multi-agent routing,' but incorrectly describes `channels.defaults.groupPolicy` as determining which agent handles the message rather than controlling access (open/allowlist/disabled). | | docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md | Expands the `channels.defaults.groupPolicy` bullet to describe the fallback chain, but the added text inaccurately says `groupPolicy` is used 'to select the handling agent' when it is actually an access-control gate. |
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown This is a comment left during a code review. Path: docs/channels/feishu.md Line: 608 Comment: **`groupPolicy` controls access, not agent selection** The sentence states the gateway "applies the **default group policy** (`channels.defaults.groupPolicy`) to determine which agent handles it," but this is inaccurate. `groupPolicy` is an access-control value (`open` / `allowlist` / `disabled`) that decides whether a group message is *accepted at all* — not which agent processes it. The handling agent in the fallback case is determined by the default account (already mentioned in the same sentence), not by `groupPolicy`. Consider rewording to separate these two concerns: ```suggestion When no explicit binding matches an incoming message, the gateway falls back to the **default account** (configured via `channels.feishu.defaultAccount` or the first configured account) to select the handling agent. The **default group policy** (`channels.defaults.groupPolicy`) then determines whether the message is accepted (`open`/`allowlist`/`disabled`). The resulting canonical session key (e.g., `feishu:g-{chatId}` for groups) reflects the final routing destination but does not encode which rule — binding or fallback — was responsible. ``` How can I resolve this? If you propose a fix, please make it concise. --- This is a comment left during a code review. Path: docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md Line: 86 Comment: **`groupPolicy` selects access, not the handling agent** The added sentence "the gateway applies this default policy to **select the handling agent**" misrepresents what `groupPolicy` does. As confirmed by the source implementation in `src/security/dm-policy-shared.ts` and `src/security/audit-channel.ts`, `groupPolicy` is an access-control gate (`open` / `allowlist` / `disabled`) — it determines whether a group message is allowed through, not which agent it is dispatched to. Agent selection in the fallback case is governed by `defaultAccount`, not `groupPolicy`. ```suggestion - `channels.defaults.groupPolicy`: fallback group policy when a provider-level `groupPolicy` is unset. Accepted values are `open`, `allowlist`, and `disabled`; this policy controls whether inbound group messages are accepted when no explicit binding matches, not which agent handles them. The session key's canonical form reflects the final destination but does not indicate whether routing matched a binding or the fallback chain. ``` How can I resolve this? If you propose a fix, please make it concise. `````
